Take an even grip and reach the arms without losing trunk control.
For a single-arm row, stabilize the pelvis and choose a load you can move without twisting.
steps: Draw the elbow or elbows back along the intended row path.
Move the shoulder blades with control rather than shrugging the neck.
Pause at a comfortable finish without lifting off a chest pad or leaning farther backward.
Reach forward slowly while keeping the same supported or braced torso position.
exercises.breathing: Exhale while rowing and inhale through the controlled reach.
exercises.target: Latissimus dorsi (lats); Middle trapezius; Rhomboids (beneath trapezius)
exercises.why: Unsupported bent-over row: spinal extensors and abdominal bracing hold the torso still.
safetyTips: Set your support or foot brace before taking cable or free-weight tension.
Keep the torso controlled; end the set if you cannot maintain your chosen back position.
injuryPrevention: Use a lighter load to learn the row without torso momentum.
For single-arm rows, use a stable hand support if balance or rotation limits control.
mistakes: Heaving the chest upward: reduce weight and keep the torso steady.
Twisting toward the lifting arm: resist rotation through the trunk.
Shrugging every pull: move the elbow back without crowding the neck.

exercises.name: Biceps curl
setup: Choose the prescribed grip and a load that does not require torso momentum.
Stand steadily or adjust the seat and upper-arm support for the named variation.
Begin with wrists aligned and the upper arms in the intended position.
steps: Bend the elbows to bring the weight toward the shoulders without swinging.
Use palms up for a standard curl, thumbs up for a hammer curl, or the prescribed pronated grip.
For Zottman curls, rotate to a palms-down grip for the controlled lowering phase.
Lower slowly to a comfortable elbow extension while holding the upper-arm position.
exercises.breathing: Exhale as the elbows bend and inhale while lowering.
exercises.why: Supinated elbow curl. Forearm muscles stabilize the wrist; the torso stays still.
safetyTips: Keep the wrist aligned with the forearm and avoid forcing a painful grip angle.
For supported curls, fit the pad to your upper arm and avoid snapping into full elbow extension.
injuryPrevention: Use an angled or neutral grip if a straight bar strains the wrist.
Build load gradually while preserving a controlled lowering phase.
mistakes: Swinging the torso: reduce the load.
Driving elbows forward to finish: keep the upper arms in the intended position.
Dropping rapidly into the bottom: slow down before the elbow reaches its limit.

exercises.name: Bicycle crunch
setup: Choose the named floor, decline, hanging, cable or machine position.
Support the body or establish a secure hang, and set a comfortable starting range.
Keep the neck relaxed and choose a leg position or lever length that permits pelvic control.
steps: Lie on a padded floor with knees bent and hands lightly supporting, not pulling, the head.
Curl and rotate the trunk toward one bent knee while the opposite leg reaches only as far as pelvic control permits.
Return smoothly and alternate sides without jerking the neck.
Shorten the leg reach if the back arches or the movement becomes a rapid pedal.
exercises.breathing: Exhale through the curl or lift and inhale during the controlled return.
exercises.why: Trunk flexion and rotation with alternating hip flexion.
safetyTips: Use a range you can control without neck strain or an uncomfortable pull in the lower back.
For hanging versions, check the grip and overhead support before lifting the legs.
injuryPrevention: Start with bent knees or a shorter lever if you cannot control the pelvis.
Exhale through the effort and end the set when trunk control is lost.
mistakes: Pulling on the head: keep the hands light and move through the trunk.
Swinging the legs: slow down or use a supported version.
Arching the lower back to reach farther: shorten the range or lever.

exercises.name: Bodyweight deep squat
setup: Choose the named bodyweight, front-loaded, back-loaded or guided-machine setup.
Set feet in a comfortable stance and establish stable whole-foot pressure.
Fit the prescribed support and test safeties or machine catches before adding resistance.
steps: Bend the knees and hips together while keeping the trunk controlled.
Lower only as far as the feet and pelvis remain stable and the movement is comfortable.
Press through the whole foot to stand without letting the knees collapse inward.
Finish tall without snapping the knees backward, then repeat or re-rack safely.

Use a stance that allows the knees to track in the same general direction as the toes.
mistakes: Heels lifting or weight tipping forward: adjust stance, depth or load.
Knees collapsing inward: slow down and maintain foot pressure.
Forcing depth after the pelvis or back loses position: shorten the range.

exercises.name: Bodyweight dip
setup: Use stable dip bars, or adjust the seat and handles on the prescribed dip machine.
Choose assistance or a light machine load that allows a controlled descent.
Use the intended steps and handles to mount, and establish active shoulder support.
steps: Bend the elbows and lower only through a comfortable shoulder range.
Keep the neck relaxed and the wrists controlled.
Extend the elbows to raise the body or press the machine handles down without bouncing.
Control the return and use the designated steps or re-rack procedure to finish.

mistakes: Dropping rapidly into the bottom: slow the lowering phase.
Shrugging or hanging passively: maintain active shoulder support.
Forcing extra depth: shorten the range rather than chasing an arbitrary elbow angle.
exercises.equipmentNotes: Use stable dip bars or the prescribed assisted dip station. Free dip bars and a seated dip machine are different setups.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat Jumps

Choose a low jump height that allows stable knee and foot alignment.
steps: Lower into a controlled squat and drive upward through the feet.
Leave the floor without throwing the trunk backward.
Land softly by bending through the hips, knees and ankles.
Reset balance before the next repetition and stop before landings become uncontrolled.

safetyTips: Use a clear, nonslip landing area and begin with low bodyweight jumps.
Land softly through the hips, knees and ankles; stop before fatigue changes landing control.
injuryPrevention: Practice quiet landings before increasing jump height or speed.
Use a controlled squat instead if repeated landings cause joint pain.
mistakes: Landing with rigid knees: absorb the landing through a comfortable bend.
Knees collapsing inward: reduce jump height and control alignment.
Rushing consecutive jumps: reset balance between repetitions.

Use a stride and range that allow the knee and foot to stay aligned without pain.

Knee collapsing inward: slow the movement and stabilize the foot.
Dropping rapidly or losing balance on the return: use hand support and a shorter range.

exercises.name: Upright Row
setup: Choose the prescribed bar, cable or dumbbell grip that allows comfortable wrists.
Stand with feet stable and the load close in front of the thighs.
Use a light load and decide on a comfortable lift height before starting.
steps: Bend the elbows and guide them outward as the load rises close to the torso.
Stop before the shoulder feels compressed or the wrists fold awkwardly.
Keep the torso steady rather than heaving the hips.
Lower slowly along the same close path and repeat without forcing additional height.
exercises.breathing: Exhale on the lift and inhale on the return.
safetyTips: Use a comfortable grip and stop the lift before the shoulder feels compressed.
Keep the load close without wrenching the wrists into an awkward bend.
injuryPrevention: Begin with a low lift height and increase range only while comfortable.
Choose a cable, dumbbell or wider grip if a fixed bar position does not suit your shoulders.
mistakes: Pulling elbows as high as possible: stop at a comfortable height.
Heaving the hips: lower the load.
Bending wrists to lift farther: keep the hands aligned with the forearms.
exercises.equipmentNotes: Use the prescribed bodyweight support or equipment variation. Check the original program when its exercise label does not specify the apparatus.

exercises.name: V-Ups
setup: Choose the named floor, decline, hanging, cable or machine position.
Support the body or establish a secure hang, and set a comfortable starting range.
Keep the neck relaxed and choose a leg position or lever length that permits pelvic control.
steps: Perform the named trunk or hip action with a controlled pelvis.
For crunches and sit-ups, curl the ribs toward the pelvis; for reverse crunches, curl the pelvis toward the ribs.
For leg raises, raise the thighs without swinging; for bicycles or V-ups, coordinate the specified alternating or combined movement.
Lower slowly and stop the range before the back arches or momentum takes over.
exercises.breathing: Exhale through the curl or lift and inhale during the controlled return.
exercises.why: Combined trunk and hip flexion brings the torso and legs together.
safetyTips: Use a range you can control without neck strain or an uncomfortable pull in the lower back.
For hanging versions, check the grip and overhead support before lifting the legs.
injuryPrevention: Start with bent knees or a shorter lever if you cannot control the pelvis.
Exhale through the effort and end the set when trunk control is lost.
mistakes: Pulling on the head: keep the hands light and move through the trunk.
Swinging the legs: slow down or use a supported version.
Arching the lower back to reach farther: shorten the range or lever.
exercises.equipmentNotes: Use the prescribed bodyweight support or equipment variation. Check the original program when its exercise label does not specify the apparatus.

setup: Choose the named stepping direction, split stance or approved step platform.
Start with bodyweight or a light load and use a stable hand support when needed.
Set a stride or step height that permits controlled foot, knee and pelvic alignment.
steps: Transfer weight onto the working leg and bend through the hip and knee.
For lunges, lower through the prescribed forward, backward or sideways stance; for step-ups, place the whole foot on the step.
Drive through the working foot to rise without a sudden push from the trailing leg.
Return slowly to the start and change sides according to the program.
exercises.breathing: Inhale while lowering and exhale while driving upward.

injuryPrevention: Start with bodyweight or hand support if balance limits the movement.

mistakes: Using a stride too long or short to control: adjust the stance with bodyweight first.

setup: Use a secure pull-up bar with a clear mounting and landing area.
Choose an overhand grip for a pull-up or an underhand grip for a chin-up; use the width prescribed.
Mount using the intended steps and establish a controlled hang with the trunk braced.
steps: Bend the elbows and draw them toward the sides as the body rises.
Lift through a range you can control without kicking or craning the neck.
Pause near the top while maintaining shoulder support.
Lower slowly to a comfortable hang, then dismount using the intended support.

exercises.name: Weighted or bodyweight triceps dip
setup: Use stable dip bars, or adjust the seat and handles on the prescribed dip machine.
Choose assistance or a light machine load that allows a controlled descent.
Use the intended steps and handles to mount, and establish active shoulder support.
steps: Bend the elbows and lower only through a comfortable shoulder range.
Keep the neck relaxed and the wrists controlled.
Extend the elbows to raise the body or press the machine handles down without bouncing.
Control the return and use the designated steps or re-rack procedure to finish.

setup: Set the seat, thigh restraint and prescribed handle; for a one-arm cable version, use a stable stance or seat.

Begin with an overhead reach you can control and a small, steady torso angle.
steps: Draw the elbows down toward the sides of the torso.
Bring the attachment toward the upper-chest region without pulling behind the neck.
Pause without leaning farther back to finish.
Let the arms reach overhead slowly, keeping the torso and pelvis controlled.
exercises.breathing: Exhale while pulling down and inhale during the upward return.
exercises.why: Vertical pull. Grip and elbow path change emphasis; forearm flexors maintain the grip.
safetyTips: Secure the thigh restraint and select a load that will not lift you out of the seat.
Pull in front of the head through a comfortable path; do not force the bar behind the neck.
injuryPrevention: Choose a grip width that lets the elbows move freely without wrist strain.
Use a lighter load if you need to lean or jerk to start the pull.
mistakes: Leaning back into a row: keep a small, consistent torso angle.
Pulling with bent wrists: align hands with forearms.
Letting the stack drag the shoulders upward suddenly: control the overhead return.

equipmentSetup.position: Sit with both feet grounded. Adjust the thigh restraint until it holds the thighs comfortably without crushing them.
notes: Lock adjustments and rehearse the intended range with light resistance before working sets.

exercises.name: World’s greatest stretch
setup: Choose the named stretch or mobility position on a stable surface.
Use padding or a fixed hand support where needed for comfort and balance.
Begin with a small, comfortable range rather than forcing the endpoint.
steps: Step into a comfortable long lunge and place the hands on a stable support or the floor as your mobility allows.
Gently explore the front hip and inner-thigh stretch without forcing the position.
Rotate the upper trunk and reach one arm upward only through a controlled range, then return the hand to support.
Ease out of the lunge and repeat the sequence on the other side.
exercises.breathing: Keep slow, relaxed breathing throughout the movement or hold.
exercises.target: Iliopsoas / hip flexors (deep); Hip adductors (inner thighs); Hamstrings; Gluteus maximus; Pectoralis major (chest)

safetyTips: Move gently through a comfortable range; stretching should not cause sharp pain or numbness.

injuryPrevention: Warm up with easy movement before deeper positions.

mistakes: Bouncing into a stretch: move slowly and ease out under control.
Holding the breath: maintain relaxed breathing.
Compensating with a large back arch or twist: reduce the range and isolate the intended region.

exercises.name: Wrist curl
setup: Use a light load and support the forearms on a stable surface or the thighs.
Let the wrist move beyond the support edge without moving the elbow.
Choose palms up for wrist curls, palms down for reverse wrist curls, or the prescribed rotation grip.
steps: Move slowly through the named wrist or forearm action.
For wrist curls, flex the wrist; for reverse wrist curls, lift the knuckles through extension.
Keep the elbow and shoulder still and stop before a forced end position.
Return under control using the same small, comfortable range.

safetyTips: Support the forearm and use a small load appropriate to wrist or forearm rotation.
Keep the movement within a comfortable range without forcing the hand into an end position.
injuryPrevention: Increase small muscle-group loads in small increments.

mistakes: Moving the whole elbow or shoulder: keep the forearm supported.

setup: Choose the prescribed grip and a load that does not require torso momentum.

steps: Bend the elbows to bring the weight toward the shoulders without swinging.

safetyTips: Keep the wrist aligned with the forearm and avoid forcing a painful grip angle.

injuryPrevention: Use an angled or neutral grip if a straight bar strains the wrist.

mistakes: Swinging the torso: reduce the load.
Driving elbows forward to finish: keep the upper arms in the intended position.
Dropping rapidly into the bottom: slow down before the elbow reaches its limit.
